_: Capabilities a reference film uses that we cannot do, or can only do awkwardly. Found by READING a film and then probing the engine, so each one names the film that motivated it and how it was verified. `status`: verified means a probe was rendered; suspected means it has not been built yet and building is how it will be settled. Rendered into docs/CRAFT/GRAMMAR.md.

gaps.name: An authored `filter` was destroyed by a motion track  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: Building the `vawe` teaser. A gradient word with a declared blur rendered razor sharp, three different ways.
gaps.why: The motion track owns `style.filter` (it writes the velocity blur there) and composed with what it found by STRIPPING every `blur(...)` out first, assuming any blur present was its own from a previous frame. It cannot tell an authored `blur(38px)` from its own: same six characters. Any layer with both a declared blur and a motion track lost the blur on every frame, `filter: none` on the element, no error.
gaps.fix: FIXED. The base is stashed beside the OUTPUT it produced, the same shape core/tracks/idle.js already used, so a fresh write from build is recognised instead of guessed at. Six shipped scenes changed and every diff was `"" → "blur(0.52px)"`: the old code was losing its OWN contribution too.

gaps.name: Origin-aware motion is not authorable  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: The outside standards (animations.dev / emilkowal.ski) name it as the strongest single technique: a thing scales from the point it CAME FROM, not from its own centre, so the motion explains the relationship.
gaps.why: `transformOrigin` is written in six engine files (core/type.js, core/parts.js, core/gsap-effects.js, core/compositions, core/layers/image.js, core/motion.js) and NO layer prop reaches it. Measured: 1 of 4,530 layers declares `origin`, and that one is a globe's route start, which is a different prop entirely and is how this was nearly missed. Every scale in every film we have grows from its own centre.
gaps.fix:
FIXED. `origin` on any layer writes `transform-origin`, taking what CSS takes: a keyword pair ("top left"), a length pair or percentages. Written as a style and never animated, because it is where the motion starts FROM rather than part of the motion.
IT WALKED STRAIGHT INTO A NAME COLLISION. A `three` globe has had `origin` as the [lon, lat] of a route's start for a long time and the schema entry said so; I read that entry and wrote the second meaning into the same prop anyway, and showcase-flight-globe failed at boot with my own error message quoting an array back at me. Dispatched on the VALUE now: a transform-origin is never an array and a lon/lat pair is never a string, so neither can be mistaken for the other.

gaps.name: `plane` silently beats `track`, and nothing says so
gaps.from: Recreating pin-583145851797705243. The continuous object carried `plane: 180` (toward the eye) and `track: 4`; the payoff frame it becomes sat at `track: 6`, on the picture plane.
gaps.why: A depth puts the layer in a real 3D rig, so occlusion is decided by DISTANCE and z-index stops meaning anything against it. The vessel at +180 covered the frame at z=0 for two full seconds. Every gate was green, the DOM reported the frame at opacity 1 with its text, and it was invisible. Found by looking at a frame, not by a check.
gaps.fix: core/fx/plane.js should refuse, or at least warn, when a layer with a depth has a LOWER `track` than a layer it now occludes. The docs should say the plainer thing first: once anything in the frame has depth, `track` orders only the layers that share a plane.
gaps.workaround: Give both layers the same depth, or drop the depth. Here the vessel gained nothing from it: there is no camera move to give parallax against.

gaps.name: A living ground can hide a dead film
gaps.from: The same recreation. It measured 2% still and motion 1.25 on `aurora`, comfortably alive.
gaps.why: Swapping to a near-static ground dropped it to 75% still and 0.29 with NOT ONE LAYER CHANGED. The aurora was contributing almost the whole number and the layers were nearly inert underneath it. The renderer's motion figure is a property of the FRAME, so a moving backdrop flatters it exactly as much as moving content does.
gaps.fix: Report the film's motion with the backdrop excluded, or beside it. `internal/scene/scene.go` measures the composited frame and could measure a second pass with `bg` suppressed; that difference is the number an author actually needs.
gaps.workaround: Measure twice by hand, once on the authored ground and once on `plain`, and read the second number as what the layers are doing.

gaps.name: A glow cannot animate its intensity  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: pin-72761350251141725 shot 3: a halo CONTRACTS toward the word across the shot. The light tightens; the type never moves.
gaps.why: `core/layers/glow.js` bakes intensity into a gradient string at BUILD (`kit.hexA(L.color, L.intensity)`), so it is a constant for the layer's life. Probed: a `vars` track on the layer changes nothing, because nothing reads a custom property.
gaps.fix: FIXED. core/layers/glow.js emits two custom properties, `--glow-i` (alpha) and `--glow-r` (falloff radius), both defaulting to 1, so the existing `vars` track drives either. Written as `rgb(r g b / calc(...))` because a legacy `rgba()` comma form cannot take a calc in its alpha. The calc form is emitted ONLY when the layer declares that var: a `calc(72%)` computes to `72%` and moved no pixels, but it changed the serialised string and eight shipped scenes reported a snapshot diff for a byte-identical rendering. Gated, the library is 105 identical, 0 changed.

gaps.name: Inverting the frame by LIGHT rather than by backdrop  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: pin-333759022406760643 spends 80 seconds on pure black and inverts three times using only light: blue streaks, an orange flood, a white bloom. The world never changes.
gaps.why: We invert by swapping a `bg` window, which changes the world. Doing it by light needs a full-frame source whose colour and intensity are both keyed, and the intensity half is the gap above.
gaps.fix: FIXED. Two ways now. `core/layers/glow.js` gained `--glow-i` and `--glow-r`, so a light can brighten and tighten over time; and the `adjust` layer's `bloom` kind grades everything beneath and screen-blends it back, so a frame can be lit by its own subject.
gaps.workaround: A full-frame `rect` with a keyed colour through `vars`. Untested.

gaps.name: Letters settling from scattered positions
gaps.from: pin-333759022406760643 shot 5 and pin-72761350251141725: a wordmark assembles from letters that were somewhere else.
gaps.why: `split` + a kinetic preset reveals letters in place with a stagger. Arriving from scattered positions is a different move and `make arsenal` returns near-misses (charOvershoot, roll) rather than a match.
gaps.fix: Unknown until built. It may already be reachable through `parts` with a per-unit motion, which nothing in the library uses.

gaps.name: Flat colour flooding the whole frame as the transition  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: pin-924363892282992611 floods edge to edge with one purple twice, and those are its two loudest measured frames (68.7 and 40.2). It costs one rectangle.
gaps.why: Nothing prevents it. Nobody does it: 0 films in our library use a full-frame colour flood as a cut.
gaps.fix: Never was a capability gap: a full-frame `rect` does it. Recorded so it stops being invisible.

gaps.name: Light could not be used to steer the eye  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: A reference tutorial whose whole thesis is animating light to control where a viewer looks. Cross-checked against docs/CRAFT/EYE-TRACE.md, which ranks the eye's targets as brighter > larger > in focus > moving and treats every one of them as a STATIC property measured at a cut.
gaps.why: Three of the four terms were decided once, at build, for a layer's whole life. A glow's colour was baked, a depth was a fixed plane, and there was no camera focus at all, so the doc named `in focus` as an instrument the engine did not have. The eye could be ranked and never steered.
gaps.fix: FIXED, all four. `--glow-c` crossfades a light's colour; `--plane-z` travels a layer in Z so it grows by approaching rather than by scaling; camera `f`/`a` rack the focus through the depth planes and every layer reacts by where it stands; and a `beam` can now feed a `matte`, so light reveals what it touches. docs/CRAFT/EYE-TRACE.md gained the section that says which knob moves which term.

gaps.name: A beam of light could not reveal anything  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: The standard track-matte text reveal: draw a beam, sweep it across the words, the words appear where the light lands.
gaps.why: Both halves shipped and could not be joined. `core/fx/matte.js` decided what could be a mask by reading the SCENE JSON for an image file or a declared gradient `bg`, a hardcoded list of four types living inside the one effect that should not care what it is masking with. A beam generates its gradient at frame time, so it was refused by name.
gaps.fix: FIXED as a protocol, not a special case. A layer type opts in by exporting `maskPaint(L, lt, geom)` and returns finished CSS, the image AND where it sits, because only the type knows the second. The next live matte source is one function in one file with no edit to matte.js. A matte source is also consumed rather than drawn now, as it is everywhere else.

gaps.name: Depth was a place to stand, never a place to travel  ·  FIXED
gaps.from: The standard slam: push type toward the camera instead of scaling it, because scale flattens and distance does not.
gaps.why: The `depth` sugar baked at boot into a static plane and the modifier wrote one number for the layer's life.
gaps.fix: FIXED. `--plane-z` multiplies the authored z through the existing vars track. The through-the-camera guard became a CSS `min()` clamp, which is stronger than the check it replaced because it holds on every frame rather than on the one the author declared.
